text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A local Moslem religious leader and his nephew were killed by having their throats slit on Thursday in the western town of Saida. "Terrorists" have blown up several Moslem buildings in the region in the past three years.
- Movement for Democracy in Algeria, led by former president Ahmed Ben Bella, said it would boycott the parliamentary elections to be held on June 5.
- Algeria to open Bellara, in the eastern province of Jijel, as first free zone to spur export-oriented business.
- Fifteen citzens found dead, their throats cut by a "terrorist group", near Ain el Hadid in Tiaret province on Sunday.
- Crude oil prices will swing around $17-$18 a barrel during the spring and summer this year but experts say oil prices will soar early in the next millennium.
